Import Modules¶

In [1]:
# Make sure you are at the parent directory
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import os

# Define MODE
MODE = "LOCAL" # Either "COLAB", "LOCAL", "EXPANSE"
if MODE.upper() not in ('EXPANSE', 'COLAB', 'LOCAL'):
    raise Exception("Invalid mode, the only acceptible are 'EXPANSE', 'COLAB', 'LOCAL'")
if MODE.upper() == "COLAB":
    from google.colab import drive
    drive.mount('/content/drive')

# --- Java 17 for PySpark (LOCAL) ---
# PySpark 4.x requires Java 17/21. On a fresh Mac the default `java` may be older
# (e.g. 15), and VS Code notebook kernels often don't inherit JAVA_HOME from your
# shell -- which causes `JAVA_GATEWAY_EXITED` / UnsupportedClassVersionError when
# create_spark_session() launches the JVM. Point Spark at a JDK 17 here.
if MODE.upper() == "LOCAL" and not os.environ.get("JAVA_HOME"):
    _java_candidates = [
        "/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@17/libexec/openjdk.jdk/Contents/Home",  # Homebrew (Apple Silicon)
        "/usr/local/opt/openjdk@17/libexec/openjdk.jdk/Contents/Home",     # Homebrew (Intel)
        "/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/temurin-17.jdk/Contents/Home",  # Temurin / Adoptium
    ]
    for _jh in _java_candidates:
        if Path(_jh).exists():
            os.environ["JAVA_HOME"] = _jh
            os.environ["PATH"] = _jh + "/bin:" + os.environ["PATH"]
            break
    print("JAVA_HOME:", os.environ.get("JAVA_HOME", "(not set -- install JDK 17: brew install openjdk@17)"))

# Root path by MODE
def find_root(markers=(".git", "requirements.txt", "data")):
    """Walk up from the current dir until we find the repo root."""
    here = Path.cwd().resolve()
    for cand in (here, *here.parents):
        if any((cand / m).exists() for m in markers):
            return cand
    raise FileNotFoundError("Could not locate project root (no .git/requirements.txt/data found)")

PROJECT_ROOT_BY_MODE = {
    "COLAB":   Path("/content/drive/MyDrive/DSC 288R/Project"),
    "EXPANSE": Path("/home/bguo3/bguo3/DSC-288R-Capstone-Final-Project"),
    "LOCAL":   find_root(),
}
ROOT = PROJECT_ROOT_BY_MODE[MODE.upper()]

# Add the root path to global system
if str(ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT.resolve()))

# Print the root path
print("MODE:", MODE)
print("PROJECT_ROOT:", ROOT)

Read Train/Validation/Test Full/Sampled Dataset From Parquet¶

In [3]:
# Set up for Spark app & resource allocation
# spark = create_spark_session("steam_reviews_machine_learning_modeling")
spark = create_spark_session(
    "steam_reviews_machine_learning_modeling",
    extra_configs={"spark.driver.memory": "4g", "spark.master": "local[*]"},
)

# Load data
paths = ProjectPaths(MODE)
if MODE.upper() == "EXPANSE":
    train = read_spark_parquet(spark=spark, path=paths.random_row_train_parquet)
    val = read_spark_parquet(spark=spark, path=paths.random_row_val_parquet)
    test = read_spark_parquet(spark=spark, path=paths.random_row_test_parquet)
else:
    train = read_spark_parquet(spark=spark, path=paths.random_row_train_sampled_parquet)
    val = read_spark_parquet(spark=spark, path=paths.random_row_val_sampled_parquet)
    test = read_spark_parquet(spark=spark, path=paths.random_row_test_sampled_parquet)

Define, Train and Evaluate All Models¶

In [9]:
start = time.time()

# ============================================================
# 1. Train + predict + evaluate ALL models in one call
# ============================================================
# fit_transform_evaluate_models() is the "one-fit-for-all" entry point. For
# every model name it:
#   - builds the estimator (build_models)
#   - fits on train_final_df
#   - transforms train + validation/test DataFrames
#   - evaluates the default metrics on both splits
#   - returns long-form + wide-form metric tables
# With keep_predictions=True it also hands back each fitted model and its
# cached prediction DataFrames so we can build per-model ROC / confusion
# matrix / feature-importance diagnostics afterwards.

model_names = ml.DEFAULT_MODEL_ORDER   # ["log_reg", "decision_tree", "random_forest", "xgb", "svm"]

all_results = ml.fit_transform_evaluate_models(
    model_names=model_names,
    train_final_df=train,   # or train
    test_final_df=val,      # or val/test
    spark=spark,
    mode=MODE,
    metrics=None,                   # None uses DEFAULT_METRICS
    cache=True,
    keep_predictions=True,          # important for ROC curve + confusion matrix
    cast_xgb_label_to_int=True,     # important for XGBoost
    verbose=True,
)

elapsed = time.time() - start
print(f"ML all models took: {elapsed:.2f} seconds")


# ============================================================
# 2. Extract reusable result objects
# ============================================================
metrics_df = all_results["metrics_df"]
presentation_metrics = all_results["presentation_metrics"]
metric_rows = all_results["metric_rows"]

# Per-model fitted models + cached predictions, keyed by model name:
#   bundles["xgb"]["model"], bundles["xgb"]["train_pred"], bundles["xgb"]["test_pred"]
bundles = all_results["predictions"]

# Feature names in the same order as the assembled feature vector (f0..f10).
# Reused by every per-model feature-importance section below.
assembled_features = [
    "author_last_played",              # f0
    "timestamp_created",               # f1
    "timestamp_updated",               # f2
    "voted_up",                        # f3
    "review_positive",                 # f4
    "log_author_num_games_owned",      # f5
    "log_author_num_reviews",          # f6
    "log_author_playtime_forever",     # f7
    "log_author_playtime_at_review",   # f8
    "log_votes_up",                    # f9
    "log_weighted_vote_score",         # f10
]

Per-Model Performance Metric Visualization¶

The cell above runs the whole batch through fit_transform_evaluate_models() and reports the shared assets (metric tables + dashboard AUC plots) once.

The sections below build the model-specific diagnostics — ROC curve, confusion matrix, and feature importance — one section per model, reusing the cached predictions in bundles[...].

Notes:

  • Feature importance is only available for tree-based models (Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost). For linear models (Logistic Regression, SVM) build_feature_importance_table returns an empty table and the importance plot is skipped.
  • LinearSVC (SVM) emits a rawPrediction margin rather than a calibrated probability, so its ROC section min-max scales that margin onto [0, 1] before binning (a monotonic transform, so the ROC curve is unchanged).

Logistic Regression — ROC / Confusion Matrix / Feature Importance¶

In [11]:
# ============================================================
# Logistic Regression - model-specific diagnostics
# ============================================================
lr_model = bundles["log_reg"]["model"]
lr_val_pred = bundles["log_reg"]["test_pred"]

# --- Build model-specific diagnostic tables ---
lr_roc_df = ml.build_roc_curve_table(
    pred_df=lr_val_pred,
    label_col=ml.LABEL_COL,
    probability_col=ml.PROBABILITY_COL,
)
lr_cm_df = ml.build_confusion_matrix_table(
    pred_df=lr_val_pred,
    label_col=ml.LABEL_COL,
    prediction_col=ml.PREDICTION_COL,
)
# Linear models expose coefficients, not native featureImportances, so this
# table comes back empty and the importance plot is skipped below.
lr_importance_df = ml.build_feature_importance_table(
    fitted_model=lr_model,
    feature_names=assembled_features,
)

# --- Plot model-specific diagnostics ---
lr_auc_roc = (
    metrics_df
    .query("model == 'log_reg' and metric == 'areaUnderROC'")
    ["test"]
    .iloc[0]
)
ml.plot_roc_curve(roc_df=lr_roc_df, model_name="log_reg", auc_roc=lr_auc_roc, dark=True)
ml.plot_confusion_matrix(cm_df=lr_cm_df, model_name="log_reg", dark=True)
if not lr_importance_df.empty:
    ml.plot_feature_importance(importance_df=lr_importance_df, model_name="log_reg", top_n=15, dark=True)
else:
    print("log_reg: no native feature importance (linear model) -- skipping importance plot.")

Support Vector Machine — ROC / Confusion Matrix / Feature Importance¶

In [15]:
# ============================================================
# Support Vector Machine (LinearSVC) - model-specific diagnostics
# ============================================================
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.ml.functions import vector_to_array

svm_model = bundles["svm"]["model"]
svm_val_pred = bundles["svm"]["test_pred"]

# --- Build model-specific diagnostic tables ---
# LinearSVC has no probability column, only a rawPrediction margin. The ROC
# builder bins scores into [0, 1], so we min-max scale the positive-class
# margin onto [0, 1]. Scaling is monotonic, so the ROC curve (which depends
# only on the ranking of scores) is unchanged.
svm_scored = svm_val_pred.withColumn(
    "svm_pos_margin", vector_to_array(F.col(ml.RAW_PREDICTION_COL))[1].cast("double")
)
_svm_bounds = svm_scored.select(
    F.min("svm_pos_margin").alias("lo"),
    F.max("svm_pos_margin").alias("hi"),
).first()
svm_scored = svm_scored.withColumn(
    "svm_score",
    (F.col("svm_pos_margin") - F.lit(_svm_bounds["lo"]))
    / F.lit(_svm_bounds["hi"] - _svm_bounds["lo"]),
)

svm_roc_df = ml.build_roc_curve_table(
    pred_df=svm_scored,
    label_col=ml.LABEL_COL,
    score_col="svm_score",
)
svm_cm_df = ml.build_confusion_matrix_table(
    pred_df=svm_val_pred,
    label_col=ml.LABEL_COL,
    prediction_col=ml.PREDICTION_COL,
)
# Linear model: featureImportances is unavailable, so this table is empty.
svm_importance_df = ml.build_feature_importance_table(
    fitted_model=svm_model,
    feature_names=assembled_features,
)

# --- Plot model-specific diagnostics ---
svm_auc_roc = (
    metrics_df
    .query("model == 'svm' and metric == 'areaUnderROC'")
    ["test"]
    .iloc[0]
)
ml.plot_roc_curve(roc_df=svm_roc_df, model_name="svm", auc_roc=svm_auc_roc, dark=True)
ml.plot_confusion_matrix(cm_df=svm_cm_df, model_name="svm", dark=True)
if not svm_importance_df.empty:
    ml.plot_feature_importance(importance_df=svm_importance_df, model_name="svm", top_n=15, dark=True)
else:
    print("svm: no native feature importance (linear model) -- skipping importance plot.")
